newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends weaker, off day's lows.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends weaker, off day's lows.

text.p: Leading UK shares slipped on Wednesday as growing worries about higher interest rates and fears of a protracted decline on Wall Street sent investors running for cover, dealers said.
The benchmark FTSE 100 share index closed 11.5 points lower at 4,236.6, having fallen as low as 4,219.0 at midday in a sharp futures-led decline. Decliners narrowly beat advancers 54 to 43.
The market got off to a firmer start initially, climbing as high as 4,266.2, tracking a modest recovery on Wall Street.
"We saw some selective buying early, but then the buyers just withdrew," said one trader.
"There's a lot of cash just waiting for the right moment," he said. "I think we'll see some more weakness, but I think we'll see (buyers) come back in on a selective basis."

Yet investors remained nervous ahead of key U.S. employment data, due for release on Friday. Any sign of strength in the report will be viewed as confirmation that the last week's move to raise short-term U.S. rates was not a one-off measure, dealers said.

"In New York, the bull has developed into a huge stomping creature and (Federal Reserve chairman Alan) Greenspan is trying to tame it. We don't think (tightening by) 25 basis points is going to do the job," said another dealer. "We're looking for a couple more rate increases."
Stock strategist David Aserkoff of Credit Suisse First Boston, who was also forecasting more rate hikes by the Fed, said he had advised clients to raise cash levels at the expense of equities.
"I'd say we're at or very close to the end of the correction in the U.S. and in UK and European markets," said Aserkoff, who cut his mid-year target for the FTSE 100 to 4,200 from 4,425.
"But just because they stop going down doesn't mean they'll start going up," he added. "The ongoing potential for the Fed to tighten further will bedevil the markets through the second quarter."
Yet many technical analysts say they see scope for a further drop, perhaps as low as 3,800 on the FTSE 100.
"Our recommendation is to sell into strength up to July and then keep out (of the market)," said Chris Chaitow, technical
Among individual features, shares in EMI Plc extended Tuesday's gains, rising 15-1/2p to 1159-1/2, on upbeat comments from NatWest Securities.

Shares in Orange Plc firmed 1-1/2p to 208-1/2, after the mobile 'phone operator said its subscriber base rose 109,000 to 894,000 in the first quarter of 1997. Brokerage Morgan Stanley upgraded the stock to "outperform" from "neutral," with a price target of 235p.
Among second-liners, shares in UK dairy companies firmed as ABN AMRO Hoare Govett issued a positive review of the sector, dealers said.

They said the broker's report said margins in the dairy industry had fallen far enough and the outlook for the future was brighter. It restated "buy" recommendations on Unigate Plc, which rose 2-1/2p to 452-1/2, and on Dairy Crest Plc, which added 8p to 208-1/2. The firm also repeated a "buy" rating on Northern Foods Plc, which rose 3p to 208-1/2. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
